# Accuracy at full data, and robustness {#sec-full-data}

**At full DrivAerML data the baselines are a few percent more
accurate than ISLA; off the tuned operating point, ISLA is the
configuration that survives.** With every model fed the same inputs and
scored in float32, GeoTransolver and Transolver lead ISLA on surface pressure by 7 to 10% on a 10,000-cell draw, a gap
whose measured parts are laid out in @sec-deficit-anatomy. What separates
the architectures is what happens when the evaluation departs from the
training conditions. Under a 10:1 sampling-density bias ISLA's relative
frame degrades 1.2x where every configuration that centers on the sampled
points degrades 10 to 16x; under refinement it converges toward one answer
while the baselines do not; in arbitrary poses ISLA's exact
covariance is worth 6% and 19% against rotation-augmented baselines; and it
holds its accuracy across a decade of learning rate where GeoTransolver
loses several-fold (@sec-robustness-lr). Across a flow-regime boundary
nothing tested generalizes.

The metric everywhere is the area-weighted relative L2 of surface pressure
in float32 (@sec-metrics), and a ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one
favoring ISLA. Every ISLA number in this chapter's figures and tables is
ISLA unless a collapsed note says otherwise; the
program's earlier configuration, the legacy centered variant (plain-mean
center, constant length unit; @sec-mt2-variants), appears only inside such
notes, where a mechanism was first established on it. The scoreboard
(@sec-scoreboard) has every DrivAerML row with seeds and artifacts; this
chapter explains what stands behind the rows.

```{python}
#| label: setup-fd
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
mean = statistics.mean
```

## How the chapter is organized {#sec-program-review}

The chapter opens with the in-distribution standing at full data
(@sec-full-data-accuracy) and its anatomy (@sec-deficit-anatomy), then takes
the departures from the training conditions one at a time: learning rate
(@sec-robustness-lr), sampling density (@sec-robustness-density) and
refinement (@sec-consistency-bench), pose (@sec-pose-contract), the query
set (@sec-query-independence), and cost (@sec-cost). @tbl-consistency-matrix
collects the DrivAerML measurements with accuracy beside consistency, and
the axis on which nothing works, extrapolation across a flow regime, closes
the chapter (@sec-regime-extrapolation).

## In-distribution accuracy at full data {#sec-full-data-accuracy}

ISLA is not yet trained on the 510- and 1,260-case
wing rungs, which the scoreboard lists among the measurements still to be
made (@sec-scoreboard). The comparison above is fair by the criteria of
@sec-fair-comparison, and narrow: two or three seeds, one validation split
per dataset, and no test-split evaluation of the full-split models, the
sealed splits having been spent on regime extrapolation.

## The anatomy of the in-distribution gap {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

```{python}
#| label: setup-anatomy
#| include: false
qv = json.load(open(RES / "quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json"))["arms"]
eqp = json.load(open(RES / "eqprice_reduction_2026-09-17.json"))["summary"]
fh = json.load(open(RES / "formheads_reduction_2026-09-18.json"))
r_ind10 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["10000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["10000"]
r_strat10 = qv["gt_unit"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / qv["isla_ref"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"]
r_ind40 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["40000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["40000"]
pts_position = eqp["points_of_ratio_recovered"] / 100.0
r_pos = r_ind40 + pts_position
heads_gain = 1 - fh["axes"]["n_heads"]["ratio_to_h1"]
gap10, p_draw, p_count, p_pos, p_form = (1 - r_ind10) * 100, (r_strat10 - r_ind10) * 100, (r_ind40 - r_strat10) * 100, pts_position * 100, (1 - r_pos) * 100
base_impr = 1 - qv["gt_unit"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["10000"]
isla_impr = 1 - qv["isla_ref"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["10000"]
```

```{python}
#| label: para-anatomy
#| output: asis
print(f"**The {gap10:.0f}-point gap at the reference size is not one thing. About {(p_draw + p_count) / gap10:.0%} of it is "
      f"finite-sample noise that vanishes with a better draw or more cells; of the rest, about {p_pos:.1f} points are the positional "
      f"information the invariance contracts deny the model and about {p_form:.1f} point is unattributed (the *form* of the slice "
      "attention was the candidate; multi-head routing tested null at full data); none is the frame.** Each part "
      "was isolated by an experiment designed to move it and nothing else, and @fig-deficit-anatomy lays them end to end in the "
      "ratio's own units, points of GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA.\n")
print("The reasoning runs from the outside in. The scoreboard's instrument is a 10,000-cell *independent* draw of each car's "
      "surface. The area-weighted relative L2 over such a draw is itself a noisy estimate of the true field error, and ISLA's slice "
      "states, being measure-weighted means over the draw (@sec-mt2-quadrature), inherit more of that noise than the baselines' "
      "unweighted aggregates. Two instruments separate the pieces:\n")
print(f"1. **A stratified draw of the same cells** keeps the inclusion law and the token budget but spreads the cells evenly over "
      f"the surface (@sec-using-sampler). Every model improves, GeoTransolver by {base_impr:.1%}, which is the metric's own "
      f"estimator noise and cancels in the ratio, and ISLA by {isla_impr:.1%}; the excess is the draw variance of ISLA's slice "
      f"integrals, and it is worth {p_draw:.1f} points of ratio.")
print(f"2. **More cells.** From the stratified 10,000-cell draw to an independent 40,000-cell draw the ratio moves a further "
      f"{p_count:.1f} points. This is the spread of the Horvitz–Thompson weights of a uniform-over-cells sample, which only more "
      "cells or a weight-changing quadrature can reduce; retraining under an area-proportional draw buys only a few percent.\n")
print(f"What remains at 40,000 cells, {(1 - r_ind40) * 100:.1f} points, is the trained function's deficit. Two further experiments "
      "split it:\n")
print(f"3. **Raw coordinates as a diagnostic.** Appending each cell's centered coordinates and normal to ISLA's seeds, which breaks "
      f"the contracts by design, recovers {p_pos:.1f} points at 435 cars (measured on the legacy centered variant, whose frame the "
      "raw channel presupposes). That is the price of denying the model absolute position, and it is the honest cost of exact pose "
      f"invariance and sampling consistency. The diagnostic's own density factor rises to {eqp['density_factor']:.0f}x, showing what "
      "it reads; it is never a configuration.")
print(f"4. **Routing multiplicity, tested.** Transolver's physics attention routes each token through eight independent heads per "
      f"layer; ISLA routes it once. On a one-car overfitting instrument eight independent routings per block lower ISLA's floor by "
      f"{heads_gain:.0%}, but trained on 435 cars four routings score 0.975x ISLA and eight 1.017x, so the one-car ordering does not "
      f"transfer and the remaining {p_form:.1f} point stays unattributed (@sec-nb-heads435-verdict). ISLA is single-routing.\n")
print("The frame contributes nothing at the reference size: the centered frames the program measured sit within 1 to 2% of the "
      "reference, and at the scale corner the reference's excess against a rate-matched centered frame is the same few percent "
      "(the scale-corner note above).")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-deficit-anatomy
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The anatomy of ISLA's in-distribution gap on DrivAerML (435 training
#|   cars, 48 validation cars, float32). The horizontal axis is GeoTransolver
#|   ÷ ISLA on surface pressure; 1.0 is parity. The leftmost marker is the
#|   scoreboard's instrument, an independent 10,000-cell draw, GeoTransolver
#|   against ISLA. Each bar is one measured part of the gap, in the
#|   order it was isolated: the draw variance of ISLA's slice integrals (the
#|   same checkpoints under a stratified draw), the weight-spread count noise
#|   (the same checkpoints at 40,000 cells), the positional information the
#|   contracts deny (a raw-coordinate diagnostic on the legacy centered
#|   variant, measured at 10,000 cells and shown against the fine-sample
#|   residual), and the remainder, which
#|   multi-head routing was tested for and does not explain at full data (the
#|   form. The frame's contribution is zero and is marked. How to read this:
#|   the two left bars are noise the deployment can remove; the two right
#|   bars are properties of the trained function, the first of which is the
#|   price of the contracts. It does not show the HiLiftAeroML gaps, whose
#|   mechanism is different (@sec-data-efficiency). Data:
#|   results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json,
#|   results/eqprice_reduction_2026-09-17.json,
#|   results/formheads_reduction_2026-09-18.json.
#| code-fold: true
parts = [
    ("draw variance of ISLA's slice integrals\n(stratified draw of the same 10,000 cells)", r_ind10, r_strat10, BLUE_LIGHT, ""),
    ("weight-spread count noise\n(40,000 cells instead of 10,000)", r_strat10, r_ind40, BLUE_LIGHT, ""),
    ("positional information the contracts deny\n(raw-coordinate diagnostic on the legacy centered variant, 10,000 cells)", r_ind40, r_pos, BLUE_PALE, "///"),
    (f"unattributed remainder (multi-head routing\ntested null at 435 cars)", r_pos, 1.0, VIOLET, ""),
]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.4, 4.8))
y = list(range(len(parts)))[::-1]
for yy, (label, a, b, c, h) in zip(y, parts):
    ax.barh(yy, b - a, left=a, height=0.55, color=c, hatch=h, edgecolor="white" if not h else BLUE, linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.text(b + 0.002, yy, f"+{(b - a) * 100:.1f} pts", va="center", fontsize=9, color=INK2)
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK2, lw=1.0, zorder=2); ax.text(1.0, len(parts) - 0.35, " parity", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="bottom")
for xv, lab, yy in ((r_ind10, f"independent 10,000-cell draw\n{r_ind10:.3f}", 3.55), (r_strat10, f"stratified 10,000\n{r_strat10:.3f}", 2.55), (r_ind40, f"independent 40,000\n{r_ind40:.3f}", 1.55)):
    ax.plot([xv], [yy - 0.45], marker="v", ms=7, color=INK, zorder=5); ax.text(xv, yy - 0.25, lab, ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK2, path_effects=halo())
ax.text(0.9, -0.85, "the frame: 0 points at the reference size (centered frames within 1 to 2% of the reference)", fontsize=8.5, color=MUTED, va="center")
ax.set_xlim(0.895, 1.03); ax.set_ylim(-1.3, len(parts) + 0.2)
ax.set_xticks([0.90, 0.92, 0.94, 0.96, 0.98, 1.00, 1.02])
ax.set_xlabel("GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, surface pressure error [–]  (1 = parity; higher favors ISLA)")
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels([p[0] for p in parts], fontsize=9); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.set_title("where the DrivAerML gap comes from, measured piece by piece")
plt.show()
```

The consequence for deployment is the recommendation of @sec-using-sampler:
use the stratified draw, or more cells. The consequence for the
architecture is stated in the thesis: a couple of points bought with the
contracts, and under a point that no tested mechanism explains.
The 25 to 28% at 35 HiLift cases is a different mechanism, the mesher
pattern where geometries recur (@sec-data-efficiency), and is priced there.

## Learning-rate robustness {#sec-robustness-lr}

**ISLA trains at the protocol rate on a new dataset without a sweep; on the
configuration it was measured on, its error across a decade of learning
rate stays close to its best where GeoTransolver's grows several-fold one
grid step above its best rate.** The measurement was made on the legacy
centered variant and is being re-measured on ISLA
(@sec-nb-refprops-prereg); its grid, figure and numbers are in the collapsed
note. Robustness to learning rate is not robustness to seed: ISLA has the
larger seed-to-seed prediction spread on both datasets (@sec-shared-floor).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The learning-rate grid (diagnostic, legacy centered variant)"}
```{python}
#| label: setup-lr
#| include: false
SW = RES / "mixedres_training_2026-07-31" / "sweep"
iw = json.load(open(RES / "instrument_wave_reduction_2026-09-01.json"))
round3 = json.load(open(SW / "round3_reduction.json"))
mt2_const = json.load(open(SW / "mt2_v3c_reduction.json"))
mega = json.load(open(SW / "mega_reduction.json"))
hl = json.load(open(RES / "highlift_wave_reduction.json"))
dr = {"gt": {}, "isla_cg": {}}
for arch, code in (("gt", "gt"), ("isla_cg", "mt2")):
    for lr_key, lr in (("lr1e3", 1e-3), ("lr1e2", 1e-2)):
        dr[arch][lr] = [iw[f"iw_{code}_{lr_key}_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)]
dr["gt"][3e-3] = [round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["sweep_metrics"]["10000"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)]
dr["isla_cg"][3e-3] = ([mt2_const[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["sweep"]["10000"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)]
                       + [mega[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (45, 46)])
hlg = {"gt": {}, "isla_cg": {}}
for arch, code in (("gt", "gt"), ("isla_cg", "mt2")):
    hlg[arch][1e-3] = [hl[f"{code}_hl_lr1_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)]
    hlg[arch][3e-3] = [hl[f"{code}_hl_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)]
def lr_stats(grid):
    means = {lr: mean(v) for lr, v in grid.items()}; best = min(means, key=means.get)
    above = [lr for lr in sorted(means) if lr > best]
    step = means[above[0]] / means[best] if above else None
    seed_step = [v / means[best] for v in grid[above[0]]] if above else []
    return dict(worst_over_best=max(means.values()) / min(means.values()), step=step, seed_step=seed_step, best=best)
LR = {name: {arch: lr_stats(g[arch]) for arch in g} for name, g in (("dr", dr), ("hl", hlg))}
```

```{python}
#| label: para-lr-lead
#| output: asis
gd, gh = LR["dr"]["gt"], LR["hl"]["gt"]; idr, ihl = LR["dr"]["isla_cg"], LR["hl"]["isla_cg"]
seed_lo = min(gd["seed_step"] + gh["seed_step"]); seed_hi = max(gd["seed_step"] + gh["seed_step"])
print(f"**Across the learning-rate grid ISLA's worst point is within {idr['worst_over_best']:.2f}x of its best on DrivAerML and "
      f"{ihl['worst_over_best']:.2f}x on HiLiftAeroML, while GeoTransolver degrades {min(gd['step'], gh['step']):.1f} to "
      f"{max(gd['step'], gh['step']):.1f}x by seed mean one grid step above its best rate ({seed_lo:.0f} to {seed_hi:.0f}x by "
      "individual seed).** The grid is {1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2} on DrivAerML and {1e-3, 3e-3} on HiLift, two seeds per cell (three to "
      "five in the DrivAerML 3e-3 cell), ISLA's legacy centered variant, bfloat16 evaluation on identical points (valid for a "
      "within-grid comparison; @sec-metrics).")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-lr-robustness
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Learning-rate robustness at full data. Validation surface-pressure error
#|   (log axis, bfloat16 evaluation) against learning rate for GeoTransolver
#|   (red circles) and ISLA's legacy centered variant (open light-blue squares; diagnostic);
#|   small markers are seeds, lines join seed means. Left: DrivAerML, 435
#|   training cars. Right: the HiLiftAeroML full split, 1,260 training cases.
#|   The GeoTransolver lanes consumed the physical freestream velocity, which
#|   is neutral on DrivAerML and the input hazard of @sec-part-baseline on
#|   HiLiftAeroML, so the right panel's red series is not a comparison with
#|   ISLA. How to read this: the vertical spread of one color across the grid
#|   is that architecture's sensitivity to learning rate. It does not show
#|   seed sensitivity at a fixed rate, which is larger for ISLA
#|   (@sec-shared-floor), nor any rate below 1e-3. Instrument: bfloat16
#|   evaluation on identical points. Data:
#|   results/instrument_wave_reduction_2026-09-01.json,
#|   results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/{round3,mt2_v3c,mega}_reduction.json,
#|   results/highlift_wave_reduction.json.
#| code-fold: true
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.0, 4.6), sharey=True)
for ax, grid, title in zip(axs, (dr, hlg), ("DrivAerML, 435 training cars", "HiLiftAeroML full split, 1,260 training cases")):
    for arch in ("gt", "isla_cg"):
        c = STYLE[arch]["color"]; lrs = sorted(grid[arch]); means = [mean(grid[arch][lr]) for lr in lrs]
        ax.plot(lrs, means, **series_kwargs(arch, lw=2.0, ms=7, label=("ISLA, legacy centered variant (diagnostic)" if arch == "isla_cg" else STYLE[arch]["label"])), zorder=3)
        for lr in lrs:
            ax.scatter([lr] * len(grid[arch][lr]), grid[arch][lr], color=c, s=16, alpha=0.9, zorder=4)
        xm = (lrs[-2] * lrs[-1]) ** 0.5; ym = (means[-2] * means[-1]) ** 0.5
        txt = f"{'ISLA, legacy centered variant' if arch == 'isla_cg' else STYLE[arch]['label']}\nworst ÷ best = {max(means) / min(means):.2f}x"
        off = (-10, 6, "right", "bottom") if arch == "gt" else ((6, -10, "left", "top") if ax is axs[0] else (0, -12, "center", "top"))
        ax.annotate(txt, (xm, ym), xytext=off[:2], textcoords="offset points", color=c, fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold",
                    ha=off[2], va=off[3], path_effects=halo())
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks(sorted(grid["gt"])); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{lr:g}" for lr in sorted(grid["gt"])]); ax.set_xlim(6e-4, 1.6e-2)
    ax.set_xlabel("learning rate [–]"); ax.set_title(title, pad=8)
    ax.grid(True, which="major"); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
axs[0].set_yticks([0.03, 0.04, 0.06, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8]); axs[0].set_yticklabels(["0.03", "0.04", "0.06", "0.10", "0.20", "0.40", "0.80"])
axs[0].set_ylim(0.026, 1.0)
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_ylabel("surface pressure error, area-weighted relative L2 [–]")
    ax.yaxis.set_tick_params(labelleft=True)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Sampling-density robustness {#sec-robustness-density}

**Under a 10:1 spatially biased sampling density ISLA's relative frame
degrades 1.2x; every configuration that centers its coordinates on the
sampled points, GeoTransolver and Transolver among them, degrades 10 to
16x.** The probe evaluates a trained DrivAerML
model on the 48 validation cars with surface points drawn ten times more
densely at the front of the car than at the back, with exact
Horvitz–Thompson measure weights so that every weighted integral is
unbiased; the readout is the error under the biased draw divided by the
same model's error under uniform sampling at 10,000 points. A ratio of 1
means the prediction depends only on the surface and not on how it was
sampled. Every ratio states its frame: the *sample frame* centers each
model's coordinates on the biased sample itself, which is what a biased
mesher delivers and what ISLA computes inside the model; the *pool frame*
hands a model an unbiased center it would not have in deployment and
appears only where it is the value on file.

The mechanism is the one taught in @sec-mt2-frame. ISLA has no origin: translation invariance comes from
point-to-anchor differences and the length unit is the total surface
measure, an integral the biased draw estimates without bias. GeoTransolver
and Transolver consume coordinates centered by the datapipe on the plain
mean of the sampled points, which moves by 0.94 RMS radii under the 10:1
bias, and every downstream quantity moves with it.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-density
#| output: asis
rows = [("ISLA", MR["isla_relative_frame_meas"]),
        ("GeoTransolver", MR["geotransolver_unit"]),
        ("Transolver", MR["transolver_unit"]),
        ("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", MR["geotransolver_unit_mw"]),
        ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", MR["transolver_unit_mw"])]
out = "| configuration | uniform 10,000-cell error | biased ÷ uniform, sample frame |\n|---|---:|---:|\n"
for lab, r in rows:
    out += f"| {lab} | {r['in_family']:.4f} | {r['density_factor']:.2f}x |\n"
for lab, k in (("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)", "mwaw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"),
               ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)", "mwaw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3")):
    r = MW[k]
    out += f"| {lab} | {r['infamily_mean']:.4f} | {r['probe_sfht']['ratio_mean']:.2f}x |\n"
print(out)
print(": Sampling-density robustness on DrivAerML, float32, 48 validation cars, 10,000 cells: surface-pressure error under uniform "
      "sampling, and the same checkpoint's error under 10:1 biased inclusion with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights divided by its "
      "uniform error, input frame from the biased sample (seed means; 1.0 means sampling-independent predictions). The "
      "measure-weighted and Horvitz–Thompson-centered baselines are ablations that locate where the sensitivity lives; the "
      "GeoTransolver and Transolver are the two plain baseline rows. Data: "
      "results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json (provenance per row inside), results/mwaw_2026-09-11.json. {#tbl-density}")
```

Two things follow. The sensitivity is the **frame, not the aggregation**:
measure-weighted pooling leaves the baselines at 14 to 16x, and an unbiased
center alone brings them to 1.03 to 1.04x. ISLA's residual 1.2x is the
**variance of its measure-weighted routing integral** under a 10:1 sample,
not a frame effect. The scope is one bias pattern at one ratio on one
dataset; the benchmark below varies the sampling law and the count.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What the legacy centered variant and the weights-off ablation add (diagnostic)"}

## Consistency under refinement and across samplers {#sec-consistency-bench}

**No configuration gives the same field under a different sampling of the
same surface at 10,000 cells; ISLA's relative frame converges toward it as
the sample grows, and GeoTransolver and Transolver do not.**
The consistency benchmark asks the question the principle of @sec-principle
poses: does a model converge to one field under refinement, and to the same
field under two sampling laws? Every checkpoint was evaluated in float32 on
the same validation surfaces sampled three ways from a 320,000-cell pool at
2,500 to 40,000 cells: uniformly over cells (the training convention, which
inherits the mesher's refinement), proportionally to cell area (the law a
uniform point-cloud generator would produce), and with the 10:1 bias; each
draw carries exact Horvitz–Thompson weights, so a measure-consistent model
sees the same integral under all three.

```{python}
#| label: fig-consistency-curves
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Convergence toward consistency. Each panel plots an architecture's
#|   surface-pressure error divided by the same architecture's error under
#|   uniform sampling at 40,000 cells, against the number of sampled cells,
#|   for three samplers (columns) and two validation sets (rows); a curve
#|   approaching 1 converges to the uniform-sampling answer. Uniform sampling
#|   (left) converges for every arm. Under the area-proportional sampler
#|   (middle) the ISLA arms fall toward 1 while the baselines are
#|   flat. Under the 10:1 bias (right) the ISLA arms approach the uniform
#|   answer at 40,000 cells. ISLA was benchmarked from
#|   10,000 cells, so its curves start there. How to read this: only the
#|   trend with count is interpretable under the area sampler, whose weights
#|   span four decades and leave refined regions unsampled at small counts,
#|   so fixed-count values there mix information loss with model dependence.
#|   Seed means over two seeds; float32; each checkpoint under its training
#|   snapshot. Data: results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json,
#|   results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json.
#| code-fold: true
B = json.load(open(RES / "consistency_bench" / "consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json"))
A = dict(B["arms"]); COUNTS = [str(c) for c in B["counts"]]
A.update(json.load(open(RES / "consistency_bench" / "consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json"))["arms"])
ROWS = [
 ("DrivAerML, 48 cars", {"isla_ref": "rf_dr_mt2_meas", "gt": "uw_gt_unit_lr1e3", "t": "uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3"}),
 ("HiLift, 35 training cases", {"isla_ref": "rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce", "gt": "udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3", "t": "udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3"}),
]
LABELS = {}
SAMPLERS = [("unif", "uniform over cells"), ("area", "area-proportional"), ("biased", "10:1 front/back bias")]
def err(arm, sampler, count):
    return A[arm]["table"][sampler][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(len(ROWS), 3, figsize=(10.2, 6.6), sharex=True)

        ax.axhline(1.0, color=BASELINE, lw=1.0, zorder=1)

handles, labels_ = axs[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(handles, labels_, loc="upper left", ncol=4, fontsize=8.5, bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 0.99), handlelength=2.4, columnspacing=1.4)
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-consistency-40k
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
for name in ("consistency_bench_mcenter_2026-09-10.json", "consistency_bench_mw_2026-09-10.json"):
    A.update(json.load(open(RES / "consistency_bench" / name))["arms"])
def D(arm, sampler, count="40000"):
    return A[arm]["D"][sampler][count]["pressure_l2"]
def conv(arm, sampler):
    t = A[arm]["table"][sampler]; lo = "2500" if "2500" in t else "10000"
    return t[lo]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] / t["40000"]["pressure_l2"]["mean"]
rows = [("DrivAerML", "ISLA", "rf_dr_mt2_meas"),
        ("DrivAerML", "GeoTransolver", "uw_gt_unit_lr1e3"), ("DrivAerML", "Transolver", "uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3"),
        ("DrivAerML", "GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation; pool frame)", "mw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"), ("DrivAerML", "Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation; pool frame)", "mw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3"),
        ("HiLift 35", "ISLA", "rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce"),
        ("HiLift 35", "GeoTransolver", "udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3"), ("HiLift 35", "Transolver", "udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3"),
        ("HiLift 35", "GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation; pool frame)", "mw_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3"), ("HiLift 35", "Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation; pool frame)", "mw_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")]
def table_rows(rows):
    out = "| validation set | configuration | uniform 40k error | area ÷ uniform − 1 at 40k | bias ÷ uniform − 1 at 40k | area-curve fall, first count → 40k |\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
    for ds, label, arm in rows:
        u40 = A[arm]["table"]["unif"]["40000"]["pressure_l2"]["mean"]
        out += f"| {ds} | {label} | {u40:.4f} | {D(arm,'area'):+.0%} | {D(arm,'biased'):+.1%} | {conv(arm,'area'):.2f}x |\n"
    return out
print(table_rows(rows))
print(": Consistency at the benchmark's largest count. The preregistered bars are a sampler dependence of at most 3% for consistent and at least 10% for reading the sampling distribution. ISLA passes both samplers on the wings at 35 cases and converges to within 3 to 4% on the cars; GeoTransolver and Transolver read the sampling distribution by 90% or more. The measure-weighted baselines' area and bias columns are pool-frame values: with the frame held, measure weighting makes their aggregation consistent; centered on the drawn sample their frame collapses, and holds only when the center is the Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the geometric centroid (@tbl-density). The last column is the factor by which each arm's area-sampler error fell over the counts it was run at (2,500 to 40,000 cells; 10,000 to 40,000 for ISLA). Float32, two-seed means. Data: results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mw and _rf companions. {#tbl-consistency-40k}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

print(": The similarity-gauge variant at the benchmark's largest count, same columns as @tbl-consistency-40k. Its frame is "
      "two integrals of the sample (measure-weighted centroid, RMS radius), so it converges like ISLA; the variant is a "

```
:::

Three readings, in order of weight. **Consistency in the fine-mesh limit is
a property of the measure-weighted estimator standing on a frame that
reads no sample statistic.** ISLA has that frame by
construction and shows the property: on DrivAerML its area-sampler and bias
dependence fall from +41% and +19% at 10,000 cells to +3.4% and +2.5% at
40,000; on the 35-case HiLift rung it is within 1.3% and 0.9% at 40,000;
on the fixed-angle rung it converges to +2.6% and +5.5%, still short of the
bar there. **No configuration is consistent at the 10,000 cells of the
book's accuracy numbers**, and a factor-of-ten probe understates how far
each stands from consistency, since a different mesher changes the local
density by thousands. **On the wings, whose refinement spans more decades
than the cars', the sample-centered configurations do not converge within
40,000 cells**; their HiLift rows report the distance, not a verdict.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The centered diagnostics on the same benchmark (legacy centered variant, its measure-centered repair, and the weights-off ablation)"}
The legacy centered variant reads the sampling distribution by 90% or more,
like the baselines, and its dependence is entirely its plain-mean
centroid: replacing that centroid by its Horvitz–Thompson estimate gives the
same field under all three samplers. A relative-frame diagnostic with a
constant length unit instead of the total measure is shown for the scale
choice. The weights-off ablation reads the sampling distribution most of
all.

A measure-weighted ISLA trained on the area-proportional convention and

## Pose: a contract, not an accuracy edge {#sec-pose-contract}

**ISLA is exactly covariant to rotations and translations. When
geometries arrive in arbitrary poses that exactness is worth 6% against
GeoTransolver and 19% against Transolver trained with rotation
augmentation; when every case is in a native pose, or a canonical frame can
be computed, it is a contract and not an accuracy edge.** The pose
measurement was made on the legacy centered variant, whose covariance
contract is the same as the reference's; the reference's re-measurement is
running (@sec-nb-refprops-prereg). With every DrivAerML case in its own
random pose, that ISLA, trained without augmentation, scores 0.0566 (1.01x
its native-pose error);
GeoTransolver trained with rotation augmentation scores 0.0602 (1.20x its
native-pose 0.0503) and Transolver with augmentation 0.0676 (1.31x its
0.0517). GeoTransolver without augmentation scores 0.0631 and ISLA with
augmentation 0.0578. Data:
research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_b_pose/campaign_b_fp32_2026-09-10.json.

GeoTransolver trained in a canonical frame (freestream to +x, roll fixed
from the geometry's principal axes; @sec-pose) is exactly pose-invariant at
1.01x cost. What ISLA's construction still buys is generality: it needs no
known global direction to canonicalize against and no sign-resolvable
principal frame. Where those fail, on a geometry with a degenerate inertia
tensor or in a setting without a global flow direction, the canonicalized
model has no frame to compute, the augmented model pays the 20 to 31%
above, and the equivariant one is unaffected. ISLA's covariance is exact by
algebraic construction and verified to roundoff in float64; on the trained
GPU path it holds to 3e-5 in float32 and to about 4% under bf16 autocast,
so the contract is exercised at deployment only under float32 inference
(@sec-mt2-contracts).

## Query independence and its price {#sec-query-independence}

**As shipped, ISLA's prediction at a surface point
depends weakly on which other points were sampled with it, about 7%
against 2% for GeoTransolver; the optional passive decoder removes that
dependence exactly, at a 3.0 to 3.7x cost in accuracy.** Holding a shared
prefix of 5,000 cells fixed and redrawing the rest of the 10,000-point
sample moves the predictions on the prefix by about 7% for ISLA and 2% for
GeoTransolver. The passive decoder (@sec-mt2-passive) replaces the readout
with read blocks that never write back, so a point evaluated alone gives the
same answer, to float64 roundoff, as in a batch of 10,000. Its price on
DrivAerML surface pressure, measured against the legacy centered variant
(the comparator of that study, within 2% of the reference in distribution),
is 3.5 to 3.7x at the same learning rate (0.203 to 0.211 against 0.0577)
and 3.0 to 3.3x against a 6,500-token interacting control. The consequence is a choice, not a
defect: exact evaluate-anywhere semantics at about three times the error,
or GeoTransolver-class accuracy with a few percent of sensitivity to how the
boundary was sampled. The interior task shows the same trade
(@sec-interior): the passive decode is about 3x behind GeoTransolver-volume
on interior pressure, and admitting the queries as interacting tokens
closes that and more, at the cost that the prediction at a point depends on
the joint query set, so the interior model is deployed at its training
query count (@sec-interior-companion).

## Cost {#sec-cost}

**On the path the recipe runs, ISLA's training step is at parity with
GeoTransolver's at 10,000 tokens in half the memory, and the opt-in fused
geometry kernel keeps parity at 40,000 tokens** (@tbl-mt2-cost, with the
measurement protocol and every execution path). Every kernel option
computes the same function, so no accuracy number in this chapter depends
on the kernel; what makes ISLA the smaller model is explained in
@sec-mt2-cost.

## The frontier in one table {#sec-review-frontier}

Two tables collect the DrivAerML measurements of this chapter.
@tbl-consistency-matrix is the float32 standing of every configuration at
the reference size, accuracy beside consistency, with the scale corner
beneath it. @tbl-frontier, in a collapsed note, is the bfloat16 table that
covers the rows the float32 matrix does not: zero-shot transfer to a
held-out vehicle family, canonicalized and rotation-augmented
GeoTransolver, and two-family training. The frontier is stated as a
matrix, not a column: every accuracy number sits beside the same
checkpoint's behavior when the sampling, the pose or the vehicle family
changes (@sec-principle).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-consistency-matrix
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
M = json.load(open(RES / "accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json"))
cw = json.load(open(RES / "corner_wlr_reduction_2026-09-15.json"))["summary"]
def f(v, fmt):
    return "not measured" if v is None else fmt.format(v)
out = ("| configuration | in-family error | density 10:1 (x) | pose, random SO(3) (x) "
       "| zero-shot fastback | few-shot gain from pretraining |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n")
LABEL = {"geotransolver_unit": "GeoTransolver", "geotransolver_unit_mw": "GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)",
         "transolver_unit": "Transolver", "transolver_unit_mw": "Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)",
         "isla_relative_frame_meas": "ISLA"}
for key in ("isla_relative_frame_meas", "geotransolver_unit", "geotransolver_unit_mw", "transolver_unit", "transolver_unit_mw"):
    r = M["rows"][key]
    pose = f(r["pose_factor"], "{:.2f}") + (" (augmented)" if r.get("pose_note") else "")
    out += (f"| {LABEL[key]} | {r['in_family']:.4f} | {r['density_factor']:.1f} | {pose} "
            f"| {f(r['zero_shot_fastback'], '{:.2f}')} | {f(r['few_shot_gain'], '{:.0%}')} |\n")
sc = M["scale_corner"]["rows"]
out += "| *scale corner, 512 wide × 80,000 cells* | | | | | |\n"
CLABEL = {"geotransolver_unit_512x80k": "GeoTransolver, 512 × 80k", "transolver_unit_512x80k": "Transolver, 512 × 80k"}
for key in ("geotransolver_unit_512x80k", "transolver_unit_512x80k"):
    r = sc[key]
    out += (f"| {CLABEL[key]} | {r['in_family']:.4f} | {r['density_factor']:.1f} | not measured "
            f"| not measured | {r['gpu_hours']:.1f} GPU-h |\n")
out += (f"| ISLA, 512 × 80k, width learning rate | {cw['in_family_80k_seed_mean']:.4f} | {cw['density_factor_80k']:.1f} | not measured | not measured | — |\n")
print(out)
print(": Accuracy beside consistency on DrivAerML at full data, float32, unit-direction inputs for every architecture. "
      "In-family: surface-pressure error on 48 validation cars at 10,000 cells. Density: error under 10:1 biased sampling with exact "
      "measure weights over the same model's error under uniform sampling, sample frame. Pose: error with every case in an arbitrary "
      "pose over the architecture's canonical-pose error; baselines trained with rotation augmentation, ISLA without. Zero-shot "
      "fastback: error on 99 SHIFT-SUV fastback cases never trained on (1.0 is the mean predictor). Few-shot gain: improvement over "
      "training from scratch after fine-tuning on 20 fastback cases. ISLA's pose factor and zero-shot transfer were measured on the "
      "legacy centered variant (@sec-pose-contract, @tbl-frontier) and are not repeated here. The "
      "scale-corner rows are evaluated at 80,000 cells; the corner factors are sample-frame values (the artifact also carries the "
      "baselines' pool-frame values, 4.2x and 4.6x). The last column is training cost in GPU-hours. Data: "
      "results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json (provenance per cell inside), results/corner_wlr_reduction_2026-09-15.json. {#tbl-consistency-matrix}")
```

:::

The measure-weighted rows give the baselines every advantage the principle
of @sec-principle can name, and they split the story in two. Accuracy: once GeoTransolver and Transolver
carry the surface measure in their slice pooling they keep their
in-distribution lead on both datasets, so ISLA's contracts do not buy
accuracy at the reference size. Consistency: the pooling repair does not
touch the frame, and with the center taken from the biased sample the
weighted baselines degrade 14 to 16x. Under a like-for-like frame only
ISLA's frames that read no biased statistic survive, and the frame is the
whole of the density story at 10,000 cells for every architecture. The
measure-weighted and Horvitz–Thompson-centered baselines are ablations that locate that property; the baselines are the ones
compared and are not modified.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The bfloat16 frontier: zero-shot transfer, canonical frames, two families"}

On the common held-out fastback family no single-family row transfers:
GeoTransolver scores 0.59 (0.82 with rotation augmentation) and ISLA's two
frame variants 0.95 to 0.99, against 1.0 for predicting the mean; a second
training family moves both architectures to 0.11 to 0.13. Cross-family
transfer is governed by training-data diversity, with an
architecture-dependent offset that does not change the verdict
(@sec-limits).
:::

## What is shared and what is not at full data {#sec-shared-floor}

**At full data, 70% of each architecture's residual is shared with the
other on identical points, seed disagreement no longer predicts error, and
accuracy is still rising with tokens per case; the current understanding is
that both architectures approach a common floor set by the protocol at
this token count.** Three measurements stand behind that sentence.

- **The shared residual.** Two GeoTransolver and two ISLA full-split
  checkpoints (ISLA in its legacy centered variant) were evaluated on bit-identical validation points and their
  pressure residual fields averaged point by point; the measure-weighted
  energy of the mean residual divided by the mean of the four residual
  energies is 0.71 on DrivAerML and 0.70 on HiLift (1.0 would mean
  identical residuals, 0.25 mutually orthogonal ones). Whatever the two
  architectures get wrong at full data, they mostly get wrong together. The
  probe cannot separate shared inductive bias from any property of the
  labels. Data: results/n1_noise_floor_2026-09-01.json.
- **Seed disagreement.** On the HiLift full split the per-case disagreement
  between a model's two seeds correlates with its per-case error at
  Spearman 0.15 for ISLA and 0.19 for GeoTransolver, against about +0.6 for
  both at 210 training cases. Two-seed ensembling gains only 3 to 4%. The
  same artifact shows ISLA with the larger seed-to-seed prediction spread on
  both datasets.
- **Tokens per case.** Reducing ISLA from 10,000 to 6,500 tokens costs 8% in
  pressure error, so at 10,000 tokens the error is still resolution-bound;
  at 80,000 cells and width 512 the three architectures are within about 5%.

If the shared residual is a floor, it is a floor of the protocol and not of
either architecture, and the flattening of ISLA's data-efficiency curve
toward 1,260 cases (@sec-data-efficiency) is the floor asserting itself.
The direct test, both architectures on the 1,260-case split at 20,000
tokens, moved each by about 5% and left their ratio unchanged
(@sec-scoreboard), so the statement stands as a current understanding
supported by consistent measurements, not as a result.

## Regime extrapolation: angle of attack and stall {#sec-regime-extrapolation}

**Trained on one flow regime, neither ISLA nor GeoTransolver predicts the
other.** Crossing from low to high angle of attack, or from attached to
separated flow, multiplies surface-pressure error by roughly ten for both
architectures, to a level worse than any architecture reaches from only 35
training cases inside the regime. No architectural choice tested here
substitutes for training data that covers the regime.

HiLiftAeroML ships two curated partitions along that axis. The **aoa split**
trains on 788 cases at angles of 12° or less, validates on 112 further
low-angle cases, and holds a sealed test set of all 900 cases at 14° or
more. The **stall split** partitions by flow state: 942 training and 135
validation cases labeled pre-stall, and a sealed test set of 723
post-stall cases. In each the validation set is in-regime, so validation
error measures how well the model learned the regime it saw and test error
how far it carries beyond it. Training follows the frozen protocol with
ISLA in its legacy centered variant, two seeds (ISLA
is not trained on these splits; the finding does not depend on the frame).
The GeoTransolver lanes on
these splits consumed the physical freestream velocity, the input hazard of
@sec-part-baseline, so the GeoTransolver rows are not a comparison with
ISLA; the finding, a ten-fold loss for every architecture, does not depend
on that comparison. The sealed test was run under a protocol declared
before any test case was read: each checkpoint evaluated exactly once.

The readout is the seed-mean surface-pressure error on each side and the
degradation ratio $d \equiv$ (sealed-test error in the other regime) ÷
(validation error in the training regime): $d = 10$ means the model is ten
times less accurate across the boundary.

| split | architecture | validation (in-regime) | sealed test (other regime) | d = test ÷ validation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| aoa | GeoTransolver | 0.0301 | 0.315 | 10.5 |
| aoa | ISLA | 0.0207 | 0.244 | 11.8 |
| stall | GeoTransolver | 0.0296 | 0.276 | 9.3 |
| stall | ISLA | 0.0207 | 0.260 | 12.5 |

: Regime extrapolation on HiLiftAeroML: seed-mean surface-pressure error on the in-regime validation set and on the sealed test set of the other regime, and their ratio. Two seeds per cell; the per-seed values are the lines of @fig-hilift-ood. Data: results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json (validation), results/hilift_sealed_test_2026-09-04.json (test and d, with the sealed-test declaration recorded inside). {#tbl-hilift-ood}

```{python}
#| label: fig-hilift-ood
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Regime extrapolation on HiLiftAeroML under the one-shot sealed test.
#|   Left: the aoa split (train at 12° or less, sealed test at 14° or more).
#|   Right: the stall split (train pre-stall, sealed test post-stall). Each
#|   line is one seed, joining its in-regime validation error to its
#|   sealed-test error; filled markers are the first seed, open markers the
#|   second; red circles GeoTransolver, light-blue squares ISLA's legacy
#|   centered variant (diagnostic). Each end carries the seed mean and each pair the
#|   seed-mean ratio. How to read this: from either side of a regime boundary
#|   both architectures lose about a factor of ten; the vertical offset between
#|   the colors is not a comparison (the GeoTransolver lanes consumed the
#|   physical freestream velocity). It does not show per-case statistics or
#|   any field other than pressure. Data:
#|   results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json,
#|   results/hilift_sealed_test_2026-09-04.json.
#| code-fold: true
lad = json.load(open(RES / "hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json"))
sealed = json.load(open(RES / "hilift_sealed_test_2026-09-04.json")); runs = sealed["runs"]
ARCH = {"gt": ("gt", "GeoTransolver"), "mt2": ("isla_cg", "ISLA, legacy centered variant")}
seeds = (42, 43); n_val = {"aoa": 112, "stall": 135}
panels = [("aoa", "angle-of-attack extrapolation\n(train at 12° or less, test at 14° or more)"), ("stall", "stall extrapolation\n(train pre-stall, test post-stall)")]
X_VAL, X_TEST = 0.0, 1.0
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.0, 4.9), sharey=True)
for ax, (axis, title) in zip(axs, panels):
    n_test = {runs[f"lad_hl_{a}_{axis}_seed{s}"]["n_test"] for a in ARCH for s in seeds}; assert len(n_test) == 1; n_test = n_test.pop()
    for arch, (key, name) in ARCH.items():
        c, mk = STYLE[key]["color"], STYLE[key]["marker"]
        vals, tests, ds = [], [], []
        for s in seeds:
            k = f"lad_hl_{arch}_{axis}_seed{s}"
            v, t, d = lad[k]["pressure_l2"], runs[k]["pressure_l2"], runs[k]["d_axis"]
            vals.append(v); tests.append(t); ds.append(d)
            ax.plot([X_VAL, X_TEST], [v, t], color=c, lw=1.5, alpha=0.9, zorder=3)
            ax.plot([X_VAL, X_TEST], [v, t], ls="none", marker=mk, ms=7, mfc=(c if s == 42 else "white"), mec=c, mew=1.6, zorder=4)
        vmean, tmean, dmean = (mean(x) for x in (vals, tests, ds)); up = arch == "gt"
        ax.text(X_VAL - 0.06, vmean, f"{vmean:.3f}", color=c, fontsize=8.8, ha="right", va="bottom" if up else "top")
        ax.text(X_TEST + 0.10, tmean * (1.30 if up else 0.78), f"{name}\n{tmean:.3f} on test,  d = {dmean:.1f}", color=c, fontsize=9.0, fontweight="bold", ha="left", va="center", linespacing=1.3)
    ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xticks([X_VAL, X_TEST])
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"validation,\nin regime\n({n_val[axis]} cases)", f"sealed test,\nother regime\n({n_test} cases)"], fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.55, 2.35); ax.set_title(title, pad=8)
    ax.grid(True, which="major", axis="y"); ax.grid(False, which="minor"); ax.grid(False, axis="x")
axs[0].set_yticks([0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5]); axs[0].set_yticklabels(["0.02", "0.03", "0.05", "0.10", "0.20", "0.30", "0.50"])
axs[0].set_ylim(0.015, 0.6); axs[0].set_ylabel("surface pressure error, area-weighted relative L2 [–]")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Three readings, in order of importance. **Neither architecture generalizes
across a flow-regime boundary**: both lose a factor of about ten, from 0.021
to 0.030 in regime to 0.24 to 0.33 on the sealed test, worse than any
architecture reaches from 35 in-regime training cases (0.11 to 0.15). A
model that has seen hundreds of cases of the wrong regime is less useful
than one that has seen 35 spanning both; coverage, not architecture,
governs this axis, and velocity and wall shear degrade the same way. **The
absolute errors of the two architectures here are not a comparison**, for
the input reason above. **GeoTransolver's smaller ratio is the arithmetic of
a higher in-regime floor**: the two converge to similar sealed-test error
from different starting points, and a ratio criterion rewards the worse
start. The one mechanism proposed for the smaller ratio was tested and
falsified (@sec-ood-mechanism).

### The smaller ratio is not carried by raw coordinates {#sec-ood-mechanism}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The raw-coordinate falsification test"}
The hypothesis was that GeoTransolver's pointwise raw coordinates let it
carry a learned map from position on the wing to pressure across the
boundary. The test adds those coordinates to ISLA as a side channel,
deliberately breaking rotation equivariance, on the stall split with two
seeds and one permitted sealed-test evaluation. Bars declared before
training: raw features carry the transfer if $d \le 11.0$ and sealed-test
error $< 0.245$; they do not if $d \ge 12.0$ or the error is $\ge 0.255$.

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
b1 = json.load(open(RES / "b1_raw_coordinate_discriminator_2026-09-07.json"))
def ref(arch):
    keys = [f"lad_hl_{arch}_stall_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]
    return (mean(lad[k]["pressure_l2"] for k in keys), mean(runs[k]["pressure_l2"] for k in keys), mean(runs[k]["d_axis"] for k in keys))
lines = ["| configuration (stall split) | in-regime validation | sealed post-stall test | d = test ÷ validation |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
n_test = []
for s in (42, 43):
    r = b1[f"b1_hl_mt2_stall_rawcoord_seed{s}"]; n_test.append(r["stall_test"]["n"])
    lines.append(f"| ISLA with a raw-coordinate channel, seed {s} | {r['val']['pressure_l2']:.4f} | {r['stall_test']['pressure_l2']:.3f} | {r['d_axis']:.1f} |")
for arch, name in (("mt2", "ISLA, legacy centered variant, seed mean"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver, seed mean")):
    v, t, d = ref(arch); lines.append(f"| {name} | {v:.4f} | {t:.3f} | {d:.1f} |")
caption = (": The raw-coordinate diagnostic on the stall split against the rows of @tbl-hilift-ood. Preregistered bars: raw coordinates "
           "carry the ratio if d ≤ 11.0 and test error < 0.245; they do not if d ≥ 12.0 or test error ≥ 0.255. The diagnostic's "
           f"artifact records {n_test[0]} and {n_test[1]} evaluated test cases for its two seeds; the reference rows are means over the "
           "full 723-case list. Data: results/b1_raw_coordinate_discriminator_2026-09-07.json, "
           "results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json, results/hilift_sealed_test_2026-09-04.json. {#tbl-hilift-rawcoord}")
display(Markdown("\n".join(lines) + "\n\n" + caption))
```

Both falsifier conditions fire on both seeds: the channel leaves in-regime
accuracy and sealed-test error where the reference ISLA has them, so
GeoTransolver's smaller ratio is arithmetic and not a transfer mechanism its
inputs carry.
:::

**In practice, a regime boundary must be covered by training data; a
surrogate's in-regime accuracy does not predict its accuracy on the other
side.** A few dozen post-stall cases are worth more than hundreds of
additional attached-flow cases if post-stall predictions are needed, and a
validation set drawn from the training regime overstates the model's range
by an order of magnitude. Any reported accuracy for these surrogates should
state the angle-of-attack and flow-state coverage of the training data
alongside the error.
